boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Resaca record (May 13-15, 1864) in Atlanta Campaign [May-September 1864]. The Lay's Ferry crossing is part of the frozen record's live other name; Rocky Face Ridge (GA007) and the pursuit toward Adairsville (GA009) are separate records. The live NPS page labels the campaign "Morgan's Raid Into Kentucky" and dates it May-September 1864; neither field replaces the frozen campaign or battle interval. Campaign-wide totals are context and are not assigned to this record. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force fields name the Military Division of the Mississippi and the Army of Tennessee without counts; the live field reads zero. Cox's Appendix A totals 71,235 officers and men for Johnston at Resaca, built from the May 1 present-for-duty figure and additions including Loring's division, which it says joined on May 12. Johnston says Polk arrived with Loring's division on the 11th and gives the great numerical superiority of the Federal army as a reason for his later course. Cox gives Sherman nearly 100,000 effectives at the opening of the campaign.
claims.rationale: A reconstructed Confederate total, a Union opening figure and a qualitative statement; none measures troops engaged on May 13-15 and none is adopted. The live zero is not measured absence.

claims.value: Johnston says his instructions to Hood were revoked on the night of the 14th, and that Stewart's division, not receiving the countermand from corps headquarters in time, attacked unsuccessfully on the 15th. Cox says Judah's division was repulsed with considerable loss at the angle of the works. NPS says Sherman did not fully exploit his advantage on the Confederate right. The frozen commanders are General Joseph E. Johnston and Major General William T. Sherman; the live page gives General William Sherman and Lieutenant Colonel Joseph Johnston.
claims.rationale: Attributed judgments from interested accounts and a summary; Hood, Stewart and Judah are not listed commanders; the frozen commanders do not receive automatic sole credit, and the live ranks are not adopted.

claims.value: The frozen result reads Inconclusive and the live page Indecisive. Johnston says the attacks of the 14th were all repulsed and that the army crossed the Oostenaula on the night of the 15th, destroying the bridges. Cox says Johnston withdrew that night, burning the railroad bridge. NPS says Johnston, unable to halt the Union crossing, was forced to retire.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit.

claims.value: The frozen and live casualty texts read 5,547 (US 2,747; CS 2,800). Cox says the Dalton and Resaca losses cannot be given accurately; at Resaca he puts the Army of the Cumberland's loss at about a thousand and the two engaged Army of the Ohio divisions at nearly a thousand, with fewer in the Army of the Tennessee. The inspected Johnston report gives no Resaca figure.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. Cox's partial approximations do not reconcile with the frozen Union 2,747, whose basis is not established.

open_questions: Sherman's, Thomas's, McPherson's and Schofield's reports, Hood's corps report on Resaca (read, not cited here), Hardee's itinerary for May 15, the compiled casualty returns and Sweeny's Lay's Ferry report remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC (the live battle page and the frozen Arnold rows) is one family. Cox's Atlanta (Scribner, 1882) is a second: a retrospective Union history by the Twenty-third Corps division commander, drawing on official reports and memoirs, so it is not independent of them. Johnston's October 20, 1864 report, printed in Volume XXXVIII Part 3, is a third family (interested Confederate account). Official Records Series I Volume XXXVIII is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting. Campaign-wide strength and loss totals are context, not assigned to one record.
